solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unenthusiastic, sadly rue walk by edge of mountain

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of rue walk are put out of order
the edge of the word mountain here is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone trudging miserably along a mountain ridge, not keen on the hike at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles RUE WALK into LUKEWAR, and 'edge of mountain' gives its last letter M; 'by' just places them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid water is lukewarm, and figuratively a half-hearted response is unenthusiastic.

clue.text: College with my name? That's unreal

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
'my!' and 'cor!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A student imagines a university named after themselves and dismisses it as fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'My, how you've grown!', so it gives COR, the British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horned horse is a creature of legend, a byword for something that does not exist.

clue.text: TV controller has no right to behave theatrically

indicators.note: has no says the controller word is missing a letter, which is taken out

parts.note: the remote is the handset that controls a television

explanation.surface: A TV remote with a broken button seems to be throwing a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no right' removes R from REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out feelings in an exaggerated, stagey way is to overact or play to the gallery.

clue.text: Branch fighting force finally dropped

indicators.note: finally dropped means the last letter of the force is let fall from the word

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A military unit's last stand ends in defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dropped' removes the last letter, Y, of ARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is an offshoot or division, as with an arm of a river or of a company.

clue.text: A long way to northeast: this marks progress

parts.note: miles, as in 'miles away', means a great distance
NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: A traveller heading northeast for many miles notes each sign of advance.
explanation.walkthrough: MILES + TO + NE, read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone at the roadside showing distance covered became the figure for any significant stage reached.

clue.text: Pull on bottle: one doing this is easily deceived

definitions.text: Pull on bottle: one doing this is easily deceived

parts.words: Pull on bottle: one doing this is easily deceived
parts.note: a baby draws milk from a bottle by mouth; add -er and the one doing it is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A baby feeding from a bottle, and a remark on how gullible people are.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for drawing on a bottle, with -er added, gives the word for a dupe, so the second half points back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing liquid in with the lips is the action, and a person fooled easily is a 'sucker'.

clue.text: High flyer's TV company escapade

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite television broadcaster
a lark is a prank or bit of fun

explanation.surface: A high-flying executive's television firm gets up to a caper.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a UK satellite broadcaster. The 's of 'flyer's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'High flyer' sounds like an ambitious person but is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird is famous for singing while rising very high into the air.

clue.text: Tea in group of hotels?

parts.note: cha (or char) is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: Tea served across a set of hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; IN is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels under one owner and brand form a linked series, like links joined in sequence.

clue.text: Nothing moved in ground grain store

indicators.note: moved tells us the nought shifts to a new place within the word for ground

parts.note: soil is earth, the ground
O, the figure nought, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing was shifted in a ground-floor grain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' takes the O of SOIL to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall farm tower is used to hold corn or fodder in bulk.

clue.text: Collection of stars, type to get into Sinatra standard

indicators.note: to get into tells us one piece goes inside the song title

parts.note: My Way is a song famously sung by Frank Sinatra
ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: A type of singer gets into performing Sinatra's signature song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' puts ILK inside MY WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Our galaxy is a vast band of stars visible across the night sky.

clue.text: Bloke we think full of envy

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a chap
'to us' means in our opinion, as we think

explanation.surface: A man we suspect is green with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is old British slang for a fellow; 'we think' is 'to us', as in 'it seems to us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiring what belongs to others is a synonym for being jealous or envious.

clue.text: Sound exasperated, caught by obvious error

indicators.note: caught by means one piece is held inside the word for obvious

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see
to sigh is to breathe out audibly in frustration

explanation.surface: Someone groans in exasperation at a glaring blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noun, but 'Sound exasperated' is a verb phrase for a weary breath; 'caught by' puts it inside the word for obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake made by failing to notice something is a slip or omission.

clue.text: Heading off, unnerve relative

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for unnerve is taken away

parts.note: to daunt is to discourage or intimidate

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to rattle a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' drops the first letter, D, from DAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family member, so is a kind of relation.

clue.text: As precaution, pack like this

explanation.surface: Advice to pack carefully, just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'as a safeguard'; read literally it says put inside luggage, which is how one packs.

clue.text: Missing husband, bald and stuffy

indicators.note: missing means the letter for husband is absent from the word for bald

parts.note: hairless means having no hair, bald

explanation.surface: A bald man without his spouse sits in a stuffy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing husband' removes H from HAIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A room without fresh ventilation feels close and stale.

clue.text: First to leave York, recalled longing for islands

indicators.note: first to leave means the opening letter of the city name is dropped

parts.note: the city name as written

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for longing is turned round

parts.note: a yen is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: Someone leaving York looks back with longing to some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to leave York' gives ORK; 'recalled' turns YEN into NEY. The answer is an archipelago off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago off northern Scotland is a group of islands.

clue.text: One turning out European champion

parts.note: a victor is a winner, a champion

explanation.surface: A European champion turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' here means throwing out of a home, not appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who expels a tenant from a property does this.

clue.text: A salesman brought back copier

indicators.note: brought back means the word for salesman is turned around

parts.note: rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman returns a photocopier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mimics, as monkeys are said to do, is an imitator.

clue.text: Cosmetic lacking density and effectiveness

indicators.note: lacking means the density symbol is missing from the cosmetic word

parts.note: face powder is a cosmetic
d is the symbol for density in physics

explanation.surface: A make-up product without body loses its effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking density' removes D from POWDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength or capacity to have an effect is force or potency.

clue.text: Hurry up and crush whatever this is

explanation.surface: An urgent order to hurry, then to squash something underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means go faster, as on the accelerator; literally it means tread down on the thing.

clue.text: Band that is welcome in the desert

definitions.text: that is welcome in the desert

explanation.surface: A band received warmly at a desert show.
explanation.walkthrough: The band is a Manchester rock group of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock group is a famous British band; a fertile spot with water is a relief to desert travellers.

clue.text: We get odd novel having more than one interpretation

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of these three words take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A writer finds a strange novel open to several readings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' signals an anagram of WE GET ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade sharp on both sides cuts both ways, as does an ambiguous remark.

clue.text: Rabbit doomed to be regularly lost

indicators.note: regularly lost means every other letter of doomed is discarded

explanation.surface: A rabbit fated to keep going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping every second letter of DOOMED leaves D, O, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rabbit, like a female deer, is called by the same name.

clue.text: Pronounced ability to see where we might build

indicators.note: pronounced says the word for vision is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A builder's marked eyesight helps choose the spot for a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like 'marked', but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land chosen for building is a location for construction.

clue.text: Love god's painful back

indicators.note: back means the word for painful is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: sore means aching, painful

explanation.surface: The god of love complains of a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'god's' stands for 'is'; 'back' turns SORE round. The answer is the Greek god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of desire, counterpart of Cupid, is the god of love.

clue.text: Greatly value rate for conversion, certainly

indicators.note: for conversion says the letters of rate are converted into another order

parts.note: sure, as in 'sure!', means certainly

explanation.surface: A banker certainly values a good exchange rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' suggests currency exchange rates, but 'for conversion' is the anagram signal working on 'rate' alone, with 'certainly' added after.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish something highly is to prize it.
